# Solo technical founder-operator (Ateles)

## Archetype

Solo technical founder-operator running a company and a life through a governed agent swarm

## Stack

claude CLI / Claude Code + MCP; Python; Neotoma as canonical entity store; launchd/Docker; SOPS+age secrets; self-provisioned GitHub PATs and AAuth keypairs

## Core job to be done

Operate: dispatch agents across products and life domains from one surface without manual sequencing. Govern: keep every agent identifiable, in-scope, and auditable, and get paged only on real escalations. Remember: one durable, queryable record of everything the swarm and the operator know. Extend: add a new agent or workflow as a declaration (an entity + a grant), not bespoke glue code. Trust the dangerous parts: let low-blast work run unattended while high-blast actions checkpoint for explicit approval.

## Trigger moment

The operator notices they have become the integration layer themselves: coordinating multiple ad-hoc agent chats by hand, re-explaining context every session, and unable to say afterward which agent did what on whose authority.

## Messaging — good

Speaks to: running real engineering work (code, PRs, releases) through attributed agents, not just chat; owning keys/secrets/infra and expecting to fork and adapt code; wanting a single durable memory (Neotoma) instead of context scattered across SaaS tools; wanting human checkpoints on high-blast actions (push, merge, payment, outbound message) while low-blast work runs unattended.

## Messaging — bad (anti-profile)

The anti-profile is sourced from docs/icp.md on origin/main (verified against the repo per skill instruction; this document explicitly states it is NOT derived from the README or marketing copy but reverse-engineered from a functionality audit of daemons/skills/runtime). Explicitly NOT for: teams or multi-operator organizations (the trust model assumes one operator behind every agent; multi-tenant separation is out of scope pending Neotoma multi-tenancy); anyone wanting zero-install/SaaS onboarding (Ateles is a reference architecture you fork and wire up, not a product you sign up for); single-agent users (if one assistant chat meets your needs, the governance/orchestration layer is pure overhead); non-technical users (forking daemons, minting keypairs, managing SOPS/launchd are table stakes); hosted-agent providers looking for a turnkey platform to resell.

## Ideal entry point

Standing up the substrate: Neotoma + identities + capability grants + one daemon, then adopting or replacing individual agents/skills for their own company and life — per docs/icp.md's stated documentation priority order.
